title: Heavenly Secrets Prophecy
next_chapter_hook: Just as Chen Ji was about to make out the blurred characters, the runes on the Tianji Record suddenly trembled violently. A vast and icy will pierced through the fragment, gazing upon him—the gaze of the Eye of Heavenly Dao.

text.content: The scalding heat of the Tianji Record in his sleeve burned like a brand against his skin. Chen Ji's expression shifted drastically, yet he forcefully suppressed the impulse to throw away the fragment. Within the ruined temple, candlelight flickered, casting his half-face in alternating shadow and light. The line of prophecy still moved slowly across the fragment, coiling like a living creature. 'Phoenix bathing in fire, only through death can one be reborn.' The seven characters struck his vision, Chen Ji's pupils constricted sharply, his fingertips unconsciously gripping the sleeve's edge. Mo Xiansheng had said the Tianji Record never reveals itself lightly, and now manifesting characters on its own—this was clearly an ominous sign.

dialogue.content: (Murmuring to himself in a low voice) Phoenix bathing in fire... Phoenix nirvana, reborn through flames. Hmph, you old artifact of heavenly secrets, circling around这么大弯子 just to tell me what?

text.content: Chen Ji took a deep breath, forcing himself to calm down. He slowly drew the fragment from his sleeve, placing it in his palm for careful examination. Under the candlelight, those ancient runes were visibly reorganizing and distorting, as if weaving a net of destiny for him. Suddenly, the runes paused, and a new line of prophecy emerged—'Twin calamity, sacrifice one to preserve one; false death is not death, new life is not life.' The ink still carried warmth, yet Chen Ji's breath froze completely at this moment.

dialogue.content: (His fingertips trembling slightly, voice pressed to an extreme low) Twin... sacrifice one... Chen Nian?!

text.content: The runes on the fragment continued their slow flow, as if urging him to quickly comprehend the prophecy's deeper meaning. Chen Ji stared fixedly at those sixteen characters, his mind racing. Twin—Chen Nian and he were twins from the same mother, connected by blood. False death—that was the escape plan he had been refining for three months, using the phoenix nirvana inheritance's power to fake his death during the Sect Competition, then hiding in the shadows to weave his chess game. New life is not life—if new life is not truly vitality, then what is it?

A terrifying thought slithered up his heart like a venomous snake, Chen Ji's face instantly turning deathly pale. His fake death plan required invoking phoenix nirvana power, and what was the essence of phoenix nirvana? It was burning away the old body to gain new life. But the burning of the old body required immense power of fate to propel—where would a servant disciple like him obtain such boundless lifeforce? The answer was glaring, sending chills down his spine. Chen Nian. The Heavenly Fate Key. The heavenly fate power within her was precisely the finest kindling for this nirvana fire.

dialogue.content: (Clutching the fragment shut abruptly, his knuckles white) What a fine Tianji Record. What a fine sacrifice one to preserve one. I, Chen Ji, have calculated the world, yet in the end... I cannot even protect my own sister?

text.content: Outside the ruined temple, night wind suddenly rose, making the window lattice creak, as if ghostly wailing from the underworld. Chen Ji stood alone beside the broken torso of the deity statue, candlelight stretching his shadow long and distorted, resembling a cornered beast. He recalled the secret report received three days prior—the Holy Sect had confirmed Chen Nian's location and was setting up a sacrificial formation. He had intended to use this opportunity to feign death and secretly layout plans to rescue his sister. Everything seemed perfectly seamless; only now did he realize this chess game had from the very beginning been a deadly trap set by the Heavenly Dao.

Chen Ji slowly closed his eyes, yet countless images flashed through his mind like a carousel. Young Chen Nian clutching his sleeve corner calling 'Brother'; her heart-wrenching screams when the Holy Sect took her away; their mother's deathbed plea, gripping his hands tightly, those final words 'You must find Nian'er'... He thought meticulous calculation was the best protection for his family, never expecting the Heavenly Dao had long since woven him into its scheme. His 'perfect plan' was merely a predetermined piece on the Heavenly Dao's chessboard.

choice.prompt: The truth cut like a blade, slicing apart the chess game Chen Ji had painstakingly constructed. Faced with this prophecy revealing brutal truth, how will he choose?

choices.description: The Tianji Record never speaks falsely, but prophecies only describe the surface. Chen Ji decided to use his own comprehension of heavenly secrets to analyze whether this prophecy might have other hidden meanings.
choices.visible_cost: Consume energy to comprehend, might miss the timing
choices.visible_reward: May discover hidden information behind the prophecy
choices.risk_hint: If every word of the prophecy is true, this would be wasted effort

text.content: Chen Ji coldly snorted, the sharp light in his eyes flickering and fading. The Tianji Record's manifestation never gives complete answers—this was the iron law Mo Xiansheng had repeatedly warned him about. He opened the fragment again, disassembling that prophecy character by character. 'Phoenix bathing in fire, only through death can one be reborn'—this clearly spoke of a method to break the situation, not a fixed fate. His gaze descended, landing on the four characters 'new life is not life,' when suddenly insight struck like lightning.

choices.description: Since the fake death plan is no longer viable, Chen Ji decided to completely overthrow the original plan, using the most direct and risky method to rescue Chen Nian.
choices.visible_cost: Abandon three months of hard work, expose more hidden cards
choices.visible_reward: Attack instead of defend, disrupt enemy rhythm
choices.risk_hint: Frontal assault carries enormous risk, could lose everything

text.content: Chen Ji's eyes snapped open, cold light in his gaze sharp as a blade. If the Heavenly Dao treats him as a chess piece, then he will overturn this chessboard. Three months of layout can be abandoned, but Chen Nian must be rescued. He took out the communication jade talisman Ye Qing had given him, channeling true qi through his fingertips—the Holy Sect Saint Woman's 'Demonic Path Miasma' was precisely an excellent tool for concealing heavenly secret auras. Change plans, attack instead of defend. The Holy Sect wants to sacrifice Chen Nian in their formation, so he will snatch his sister from the altar first.

The runes on the fragment seemed to sense the change in his state of mind, their glow flickering like the struggling heartbeat of the dying. Chen Ji stared at those wandering characters, when suddenly Mo Xiansheng's words flashed through his mind—'What the Tianji Record records is not a destined situation, but a source of variables. It never gives answers, but choices themselves.' Choices... Chen Ji abruptly raised his head, his pupils reflecting the prophecy's final four characters: false death is not false.

"Feigned death is not death—these four words echoed repeatedly in Chen Ji's mind. A false dead end, a true rebirth. Or rather... not life yet life, not death yet death. He suddenly recalled the true meaning of the phoenix's nirvana. When the phoenix bathes in flames, what burns away is not just the old body, but the old fate trajectory. The so-called 'rebirth' is not physical resurrection, but the reshaping of destiny. And the fuel needed for destiny's reshaping need not be others' heavenly fate—it could also be... one's own."

dialogue.content: (A cold smile curling at the corner of his lips) Excellent scheme. Tianji Record, oh Tianji Record, you've circled around so vast a distance, only wanting to force me to walk into that Phoenix Divine Fire myself. Using my life to burn my fortune, reshaping Chen Ji's fate trajectory... am I right?

text.content: Before his words even faded, the runes on the fragment shuddered violently, as if responding to his speculation. Chen Ji lowered his gaze to stare at those wandering characters, light flickering uncertainly in his eyes. If using his own heavenly fate as the catalyst, feigned death could become real; and Chen Nian, as the Heavenly Fate Lock Key, her fate was already locked outside this chess game—only by actively entering the board could he drag his sister out of the chessboard. But what did this mean? It meant every time he used the Tianji Record, he would have to pay an even more brutal price.

The candle flame诡异地静止了 at this moment, as if even the wind dared not disturb this contest of fates. Chen Ji stood beneath the broken divine statue, his aura suddenly transforming—the groveling废物杂役弟子 was gone, replaced by a lone wolf that had been lying in wait for too long. He slowly tucked the Tianji Record fragment into his chest, fingertips gently stroking those scorching runes as he murmured: "I, Chen Ji, have arranged the world, never following others' scripts. Does Heaven want to see me enter the board? I shall be the one holding the pieces instead."

choice.prompt: Chen Ji had glimpsed the partial mysteries of the prophecy, but the true choice had yet to arrive. In what manner would he face the upcoming crisis?

choices.text: "Enter the board with my body, trade my life for my life"
choices.description: Chen Ji decided to use his own heavenly fate as the price, reshaping his destiny in the Phoenix Divine Fire, completely breaking the lethal trap arranged by Heaven. The cost was that every use of the Tianji Record would require double consumption.
choices.visible_cost: "Heavenly Fate consumption doubled, life entering countdown"
choices.visible_reward: "Completely break the局, Chen Nian's fate can be rewritten"
choices.risk_hint: "If heavenly fate is exhausted, Chen Ji will have his soul scattered"

text.content: Chen Ji took a deep breath and made his decision. He took out the Tianji Record fragment from his chest, gently levitating it before his brow center with True Qi. Mo Xiansheng's voice rang in his mind: "Are you certain? Once this path opens, there will be no turning back." Chen Ji gave no answer, only slightly nodding. The runes on the fragment suddenly erupted with blinding golden light, enveloping him entirely—his heavenly fate was beginning to burn in a manner bordering on self-destruction.

choices.text: "Borrow strength to strike, draw in the external board"
choices.description: Chen Ji was unwilling to bear the heavenly fate's backlash alone. He decided to drag Ye Qing, Han Lie, and even Ling Yuan all into this chess game, intertwining everyone's fates so they constrained each other.
choices.visible_reward: "Disperse risk, multiple parties balance each other"
choices.risk_hint: "Once any link loses control, the entire game is lost"

text.content: Chen Ji put away the Tianji Record, a meaningful arc curling at the corner of his lips. Since Heaven wanted to see him enter the board alone, he would precisely not comply with Heaven's wishes. He took out three jade talismans, injecting different True Qi into each—one bound for Ye Qing, one sent to Xuanwu Sect's Han Lie, and the last one... quietly landed in Tianqing Sect's Ling Yuan's secret chamber. Since the chess game was already exposed, he might as well muddy the waters, making everyone his chess piece.

Just as Chen Ji's thoughts churned, his gaze inadvertently fell upon the bottom of the fragment—there, a line of characters almost too blurred to distinguish, as if deliberately hidden, or as if waiting for a specific moment to reveal itself. Chen Ji furrowed his brows, bringing the fragment close to the candle flame, squinting to examine it carefully. Those small characters flickered in and out of visibility; only the first few characters at the beginning were barely discernible: "...also has... not death... not life..." The content beyond was entirely annihilated within the dark glow of the runes.

Chen Ji's pupils contracted sharply, his fingertips unconsciously gripping the fragment's edge tighter. A third path? Not death yet not life... neither the life-for-life exchange he had previously conceived, nor the muddying-the-waters trick of borrowing strength, but another path no one had ever walked? His heart suddenly raced, thoughts spinning rapidly. If this line of blurred characters was real, it meant the Tianji Record offered not a binary choice, but an open-ended riddle—it had been waiting from the start for him to create his own answer.

However, before Chen Ji could fully decipher this line of small characters, the runes on the Tianji Record suddenly began to violently shudder. A vast and ice-cold Will pierced through the fragment, penetrating his brow center, directly reaching the depths of his soul. That Will carried no emotion whatsoever, yet possessed a disregard akin to gazing down at ants—as if all Chen Ji's struggles, all his calculations, were merely jokes before that Will. It was watching him. It had been watching him all along. The Eye of Heavenly Fate.

Chen Ji felt every hair on his body stand on end, an unprecedented sense of crisis spreading from his tailbone to the crown of his head. That Will was like an abyss, unfathomable; merely the act of "watching" itself caused the True Qi in his body to nearly freeze. The Eye of Heavenly Fate—the legendary mastermind manipulating prophets through the ages, the true master of the Tianji Record—it had actually, at this very moment, turned its gaze upon him, this insignificant servant disciple. The runes on the fragment疯狂跳动, as if issuing some kind of warning.

Chen Ji violently spurred his True Qi, forcibly storing the Tianji Record fragment into his sleeve while using a secret technique to seal his own aura. That ice-cold Will lingered in the air for a moment, seemingly searching for something, before finally retreating. The ruined temple returned to dead silence, only Chen Ji's heavy panting echoing. His back was soaked with cold sweat; that instant of "eye contact" had actually given him the illusion of having walked through the gates of hell. The Eye of Heavenly Fate... it had always been there. From the moment he obtained the Tianji Record, he had already been marked by it. And that line of blurred characters, perhaps was precisely what it deliberately left for him... bait, or perhaps a trial.
